exact_statement: For every Boolean F on exactly two independent uniform physical address bits X and arbitrarily many uniform data bits Y, if each positive conditional squared Fourier row is a coordinate-product law with at most two nonfair nondeterministic marginals, arbitrary marginal odds, arbitrary Fourier signs and fixed frequency coordinates, then H(S_Y|S_X)<=[3/2+(5/2)h2(1/10)]I_Y(F), sharply at the three-bit point defect, and H(F)<=[6+2log2(65/64)]I(F)<7I(F). Every integer height-two product-spectrum row with exactly two nonfair marginals has at least two fair varying marginals, certified by the complete two- and three-coordinate endpoint domains after removing deterministic characters. No actual Boolean cover with two nonfair marginals is asserted to exist, and no unrestricted weighted nonfair-count or nonproduct payment is claimed.
hypotheses: Actual Boolean F; exactly two uniform physical address coordinates independent of data
Every positive conditional data spectrum is a coordinate product with at most two nonfair varying marginals
Normalized Walsh; entropy bits; physical original-coordinate influence; arbitrary Fourier phases and odds
